title: Anchorless stagecraft — release scratchpad and warmup checklist
content:
Context / intent:
This is my personal scratchpad for the ‘anchorless’ micro-rollout strategy I want to try for small-model flips (no tenant anchors, quiet warmups). Goal is low-risk, fast validation when we flip model variants for cost/perf experiments — especially useful for non-critical hosted-api endpoints and internal QA pools.

Notes to self (high level):
- Keep cohort windows small (0.5% -> 2% over 3–6 hours).
- Avoid global pins; prefer per-route soft-weights + SDK opt-ins for a handful of customers.
- Watch quality regressions tightly (SLA: <0.5% slam in top-1 metric within 1h).
- Automations: auto-scale warmup workers when latency > baseline+20% for >10m (see infra runbook).

Quick checklist (pre-flight):
[ ] Confirm model artifact health (sha, size, quantization tag) + smoke-run on local rig (cmd below).
[ ] Ensure model-version metadata is published to catalog and rollback label exists.
[ ] Create canary route in console (name: anchorless-stagecraft-v1).
[ ] Draft rollout JSON and save to tmp/rollouts/ with clear owner + TTL.
[ ] Slack #canary-alerts with summary and escalation list.
[ ] Set Datadog dashboards for route and pin lightweight monitors.
[ ] Notify 2 SREs + 1 oncall for first 2 hours.

Priming / warmup sequence (personal preferred order):
1) Shadow traffic (30–60m) from small client set — measure decode tail latencies and memory growth.
2) Controlled sample generation (synthetic prompts, 1k requests/min) to fill KV cache.
3) Inject a 0.5% soft-weight split for real traffic; label client cohort with tag 'warm-primed'.
4) Observe for 30m, if stable -> move to 1.5% for 1h.
5) If metrics OK, proceed to 5% for 2h then evaluate for larger fraction.

Rollback/escape hatches (write these in the rollout JSON):
- Hard rollback: immediate 100% revert if 5-min P95 latency > baseline + 100ms AND error rate increase > 1pp.
- Soft rollback: revert to previous soft-weight allocation if quality drift (top-ranking metric) > 0.75pp for 30m.
- Circuit-breaker: route-level abort if memory pressure crosses 85% on any GPU node serving route.

Important telemetry queries / things to watch (notes I actually use):
- Latency: datadog query "avg(last_5m):p95(request.duration){route:anchorless-stagecraft} by {region}"
- Errors: "sum(last_1m):errors{route:anchorless-stagecraft} / sum(last_1m):requests{route:anchorless-stagecraft}"
- Quality: nightly eval set in BigQuery (evals.e2e_anchorless_v1) — compare top1/top3/LLR vs baseline.
- Cost delta: quick estimate = tokens_served * cost_per_token_variant — look at route token breakdown in console (token buckets).

Sample commands (for smoke / local):
- Validate model checksum: sha256sum /models/model-v1.safetag.bin
- Local docker smoke: docker run --rm -e MODEL_PATH=/models/model-v1.safetag.bin ghcr.io/redwood-inference/local-run:smoke /bin/sh -c "pytest tests/smoke.py::test_infer -q"
- Curl to test route (replace TOKEN): curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer TOKEN' -d '{\"model\":\"anchorless-stagecraft-v1\",\"prompt\":\"Hello\",\"max_tokens\":16}' | jq .

Decision heuristics (informal):
- If memory grows linearly above baseline in shadow -> likely cache misconfig on variant; pause rollout.
- If P95 latency increases but tail token cost decreases (i.e., shorter outputs) -> may be worthwhile; check user-visible regressions before rollback.
- For tenant-facing clients with strict SLAs, require additional warm window and manual approval before moving >3%.

Open questions / TODOs I keep forgetting:
- Should we add a temporary qps-cap per-proxy during first 2h to avoid sudden surges? (Pros: prevents noisy neighbors; Cons: can starve legitimate small-batch apps.)
- Need a script to auto-generate the Slack blurb with baseline numbers + expected SLO impact (low-effort win).
- Where to persist the warm-primed cohort list so other teams can query it? Confluence page? small datastore?

Post-rollout watchlist (first 24h):
- 0–1h: watch P50/P95, errors, memory, and any unusual GC logs.
- 1–6h: daily eval comparisons and top client complaint signals (#support mentions, urgent JIRA creations).
- 6–24h: cost delta report, model host churn, and slow-growing regressions on eval set.

Notes about pinning policy (quick):
- Avoid global hard-pins for experiments. Use feature-flag per-client or per-route soft-weights. Reserve hard-pins for emergency stable fallbacks (requires 2 approvers).
- If a tenant explicitly requests pin, create a formal ticket INF-PIN-<tenant>-<date> and export telemetry snapshot.

Heuristic examples to include in rollout JSON: (simple pseudo)
- {"name":"latency-breaker","threshold_ms":100,"window_min":5,"action":"hard-rollback"}
- {"name":"quality-lag","metric":"eval.top1_delta","threshold_pp":0.75,"window_min":30,"action":"soft-rollback"}

Scratchy timeline stub (for next run):
- 09:30 - start shadow // 10:00 - smoke synthetic // 11:00 - 0.5% live // 12:30 - 1.5% // 14:30 - evaluate & decide for 5%

Quick references I always forget:
- Infra runbook link: confluence:infra/runbooks/model-warmup
- Slack channel for alerts: #canary-alerts
- Oncall rotation: https://rota.redwood.ai/sre
- PR for runtime change relevant to this test: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/456

Random brain-dump ideas (might be worth a short spike):
- Warm-priming via small synthetic prompts that mimic real clients to pre-warm KV caches more effectively than shadowing. Need to ensure synthetic doesn't skew production metrics.
- A lightweight backfill process that replays a small portion of cacheable prefixes in anticipation of flip.

End-of-note reminder: move any winning rollout logic into a reusable template so the next experiment only needs to tweak thresholds and cohort size. Also, pair with Solutions Eng for tenant communication template before pushing wide.

-- KT
